subject: Re: AtlasMed privacy confirmation — no model learning, logging & retention path
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@atlasmed.com>, Jordan Barnes <jbarnes@atlasmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: AtlasMed follow-up — confirmation of no-model-learning requirement and next steps

Hi Sofia / Jordan —

Great to meet yesterday. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the privacy / data handling items AtlasMed raised and list concrete next steps so we can move the pilot forward. Please reply if I missed anything.

Summary of customer requirements (as I understood them):
- No training or model-tuning on any AtlasMed customer data or telemetry for Redwood models.
- PII must be redacted on ingestion for any data that will be logged or persisted.
- Logs retained no longer than 45 days for debugging traces; aggregated metrics can be kept longer but must be non-identifiable.
- Data residency: production inference and logs to be stored in US regions only (gov/commercial accounts in our US VPC).
- Access controls: audit logs and KMS-backed encryption; legal requested an attestation for audit.

Immediate next steps I can take from Redwood side:
1) Share a short formal statement we can sign that commits to no training on AtlasMed data and outlines retention and residency controls (I’ve attached a draft).
2) Fill out your privacy checklist (attached) and return — I’ll loop in Security for any gaps.
3) Provide SOC2 artifacts and a short runbook describing how we enforce the non-training policy (what systems, who signs off, how we roll back).

Action items / owners:
- Vivek: send draft statement + checklist (attached) — DONE (attached).
- Marissa: pull SOC2 summary + controls description by EOD 7/23.
- Ben: prepare short technical runbook (KV-cache, model version pinning, and data flow) by 7/24.

Sofia/Jordan — if the summary looks right, please confirm and indicate whether AtlasMed needs a countersigned PDF or a DocuSign flow. We can also provide an Export Certificate showing logs/residency configuration during the pilot.

Thanks,
Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni

vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com

From: Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@atlasmed.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Barnes <jbarnes@atlasmed.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 09:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: AtlasMed follow-up — confirmation of no-model-learning requirement and next steps

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the clear recap — that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from AtlasMed:

- "No training" means AtlasMed data (including any user prompts, attachments, or derived embeddings) cannot be used to update or fine-tune any Redwood models, whether hosted or dedicated.
- Temporary caching for the duration of a session (KV cache) is acceptable as long as it is not persisted or used for model improvement.
- PII redaction: we have a short list of fields (patient name, MRN, SSN) that must be removed prior to any logs. We'll attach the list to our returned checklist.
- Retention: 45 days max for identifiable traces is OK, but we require an export mechanism at the end of the pilot that proves no retained training datasets were created.

Regarding signatures: Jordan in Legal prefers DocuSign for quick countersignatures. Can Redwood initiate? Otherwise we can sign a PDF and return.

Jordan, tagging you for legal confirmation on the wording.

Best,
Sofia

--
Sofia Morales
Head of Data Privacy — Atlas Medical

Vivek / Sofia —

Agree with the summary. A couple of legal asks: please include in the attestation language that Redwood will not use AtlasMed data for model development, and that any staff with console access are bound by NDA and role-based access controls. We also need to review SOC2 Type II page references for the controls around change management and access logging.

If Redwood can send a DocuSign for the two-page attestation (and include the attachments you mentioned), we’ll return within 48 hours.

Jordan Barnes
Senior Counsel — Atlas Medical
jbarnes@atlasmed.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@atlasmed.com>, Jordan Barnes <jbarnes@atlasmed.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasMed follow-up — confirmation of no-model-learning requirement and next steps

Hi Sofia / Jordan —

Thanks for the confirmation. Attaching a finalized two-page attestation PDF for signature and a completed copy of your checklist. The attestation includes:
- Explicit commitment: Redwood will not use AtlasMed data to train, fine-tune, or evaluate models outside of AtlasMed-owned test fixtures.
- Technical controls: model-version pinning, KV cache TTL = session-only (auto-evict), logs written to US-only S3 buckets with KMS encryption, access via RBAC with MFA, and 45-day log retention for identifiable traces.
- Auditability: we will provide an export report at pilot close that lists storage locations and a hash summary showing no dataset export for training.

We’ve started a DocuSign envelope and you should receive an invite from dse-notifications@redwoodinference.com shortly. Please let us know if you prefer manual PDF countersign.

Attachments: signature-request-AtlasMed.pdf (application/pdf), atlasmed-privacy-checklist-filled.xlsx (updated)

Best,
Marissa
